territorial_scope.description: Adopted by the European Commission; binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

summary.short: Commission delegated regulation under the Digital Services Act setting technical conditions and procedures for vetted researchers' access to data held by very large online platforms and search engines. It requires a DSA data access portal, reasoned requests by Digital Services Coordinators, and data provider catalogues and access modalities.
summary.long: Supplements Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act) with technical conditions and procedures for vetted researchers' access to data held by very large online platform and search engine providers under Article 40(4). Requires the Commission to establish a DSA data access portal linked to AGORA, and data providers to publish points of contact, data catalogues and suggested access modalities. The Digital Services Coordinator of establishment must decide within 80 working days whether to formulate a reasoned request, assessing applicant affiliation, independence, funding, necessity, and data-protection and security risks, and determines access modalities, which may require secure processing environments. Overviews of reasoned requests are published; data providers may file amendment requests and seek mediation within five working days, with mediation capped at 40 working days and costs borne by the provider. Coordinators may consult independent experts registered in AGORA. Data providers must notify access start and termination within three working days and must not impose archiving or analytical-tool restrictions unless stated in the reasoned request. The Annex sets Commission processor duties and security measures for the portal. Enters into force on the twentieth day after OJ publication; binding in all Member States.

notes: Adopted 1 July 2025; published in the OJ on 9.10.2025 (date from the document header); entry into force on the twentieth day after publication (Art. 16), no calendar date stated in the text. The text amends or repeals no other instrument. Target_instrument_id is an empty string where the target is not in the registry (schema requires a string). Applicant researchers (natural persons), the European Board for Digital Services, the EDPS and GDPR supervisory authorities are described but not coded as entities. Minor wording points: recital 21 uses 'Digital Service Coordinator' (singular); Art. 6(4)(c) cites 'Regulation EU 2022/2065' without brackets.

‘data access application’ means the information and relevant documentation submitted by applicant researchers to the Digital Services Coordinator of establishment
‘applicant researcher’ means any natural person applying for access to data as referred to in Article 40(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, either individually, in a group or as part of an entity;
‘principal researcher’ means the applicant researcher who submits the data access application in their individual capacity or on behalf of an entity or a group of applicant researchers;
‘data provider’ means a provider of a very large online platform or of a very large online search engine designated as such in accordance with Article 33(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065
‘reasoned request’ means a reasoned request for data access pursuant to Article 40(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065;
‘amendment request’ means a request for amendment pursuant to Article 40(5) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 submitted by the data provider to the Digital Services Coordinator of establishment

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changing legal treatment was found. The only numbers are procedural working-day periods (Art. 7(1), Art. 13(1), 13(4), 13(9), Art. 15(1)) and the Art. 40(6) reference, which are coded as procedural limits, not thresholds.

enforcement.note: The text sets out no sanction, fine, penalty, suspension, revocation or blocking provisions. It refers to Article 40 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 and Article 40(6) for decision deadlines, but states no penalty regime itself.
